title: CFU vs. Direct Cell Count

references.label: Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

summary: A CFU (colony-forming unit) count measures only viable, culturable cells under the specific conditions provided. A direct cell count (e.g. via microscope or flow cytometry) counts all cells present — living, dead, or dormant.
explanation: CFU/mL from a plate count will typically be lower than a direct microscopic count of the same sample, because direct counts include non-viable cells and CFU counts miss viable-but-non-culturable (VBNC) cells and any cell whose growth requirements the plating conditions don't meet. Neither method is universally 'more correct' — the right choice depends on whether viability under specific growth conditions, or total cell presence, is the question being asked.

comparison.left: CFU: viable + culturable under the test conditions
comparison.right: Direct count: all cells, living or dead
Hemocytometer, flow cytometry, or direct microscopic count

commonMisconceptions: Assuming CFU/mL and total cell count are the same number for a given sample.
